paragraphs: The South East of England is a region made up of many county and unitary councils, from Kent and Sussex to Hampshire, Berkshire, Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. Children in care here are looked after by those councils' own fostering services and by independent agencies such as those shown above.

If you would like to foster with a council, there is now one place to start. Local Authority Fostering South East opened on 8 July 2024 as a virtual hub funded by the Department for Education and led by Bracknell Forest Council. A central recruitment team takes first enquiries and passes them to the right council, and an ambassador scheme lets you talk to someone who already fosters before you apply. Its members include Kent, Surrey, Hampshire, East and West Sussex, Oxfordshire, Medway, Brighton and Hove, Portsmouth, Southampton, the Isle of Wight, Milton Keynes, Slough, Reading, West Berkshire, Wokingham and Bracknell Forest, with Windsor and Maidenhead, Kingston and Richmond through Achieving for Children. At launch it was described as the largest of nine regional pilots in England.

The councils set it up because they had more than 11,000 children in care across the region and fewer than 3,000 council-approved foster carers. Hampshire said at the time that another child came into its care every 12 hours.

Every fostering service in the South East must pay at least the regional minimum allowance, which for April 2026 to April 2027 is £195 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £203 for 3 to 4, £223 for 5 to 10, £255 for 11 to 15 and £298 for 16 to 17. Our Kent, Slough and Bracknell Forest pay pages show what those councils actually pay. Look at the page for your own county or town too, such as Kent, Surrey or Hampshire, then speak to your council and to two or three agencies.
